support.row: Customer support, ticket triage and answering
support.unit: Conservative: time per chat. Expected: issues resolved per hour
support.design: Field, staggered rollout, difference-in-differences, 5,172 agents, one firm

documents.row: Document processing and data extraction (notes, forms, contracts, invoices)
documents.design: RCT, 238 physicians, two AI scribes: one saved 9.5%, the other had no significant effect. No rigorous study of invoice or contract extraction found

reports.design: Field RCT, 7,137 workers, 66 firms (not significant, could be up to 7% slower). The 40% drafting figure is the lab ceiling from short reports

research.row: Research and analysis (knowledge work inside AI's capability)
research.design: Preregistered field experiment, 758 BCG consultants. Outside the frontier, AI users were 19 points less likely to be correct

email-crm.row: Sales and admin email, CRM work
email-crm.design: Field RCT, 66 firms, 7,137 workers: 12% for everyone given access, 17% for those who used it. No measured CRM study found

onboarding.design: Same support field study: new agents with AI performed like agents with three times the tenure; experienced agents saw minimal gains

software.unit: Time on task; 26% more completed tasks in field; 55.8% lab ceiling
software.design: Conservative: RCT, 16 experienced developers, 19% slower (contested). Expected: RCT, 96 Google engineers. Field: three company RCTs, 4,867 developers. Ceiling: RCT, 95 freelancers, one greenfield task

wholeJob.unit: Share of total work hours, self-reported
wholeJob.design: Survey linked to Danish administrative data, 11 occupations; all-occupation mean 3%

brynjolfsson-2023-handle-time-down-8-per.claim: In the customer support deployment, AI assistance reduced average chat handle time by 3.7 minutes, an 8.5% decline from a 43 minute baseline, while chats handled per hour rose about 15% because agents also multitasked.
brynjolfsson-2023-handle-time-down-8-per.quote: Column 1 documents a 3.7 minute decrease in the average duration of customer chats, an 8.5% decline from the baseline mean of 43 minutes

source.publisher: arXiv / NBER Working Paper 31161; published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics (2025)
source.title: Generative AI at Work
source.method: Staggered rollout of a GPT-based conversational assistant to 5,172 customer support agents at one Fortune 500 software firm; difference-in-differences on administrative data

brynjolfsson-2023-15-percent-productivit.claim: Access to a generative AI assistant increased issues resolved per hour by 15% on average among 5,172 support agents, with wide variation across workers.
brynjolfsson-2023-15-percent-productivit.quote: Access to AI assistance increases worker productivity, as measured by issues resolved per hour, by 15% on average, with substantial heterogeneity across workers.

source.publisher: arXiv / NBER Working Paper 31161; published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics (2025)
source.title: Generative AI at Work
source.method: Staggered rollout of a GPT-based conversational assistant to 5,172 customer support agents at one Fortune 500 software firm; difference-in-differences on administrative data

lukac-2025-scribe-time-in-note-9-percent.claim: In an RCT of 238 physicians, Nabla users cut time-in-note by 9.5% versus usual care, while DAX users showed no significant change (1.7% decrease, CI 9.4% decrease to 5.9% increase).
lukac-2025-scribe-time-in-note-9-percent.quote: Nabla users experienced a 9.5% [95% CI:-17.2%,-1.8%] (p=.02) decrease in time-in-note versus the control group and a 7.8% [-15.5%,-0.1%] (p=.05) decrease versus DAX users, while DAX users exhibited no significant change versus control (-1.7% [-9.4%,+5.9%]; p=.66).

source.publisher: medRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.07.10.25331333; peer-reviewed version in NEJM AI (2025) as 'Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial'
source.title: A Randomized-Clinical Trial of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: Measuring Documentation Efficiency and Physician Burnout
source.method: Three-arm pragmatic RCT at a large academic health system in California, November 2024 to January 2025; 238 outpatient physicians in 14 specialties randomized 1:1:1 to Microsoft DAX, Nabla, or usual care; primary outcome change in time-in-note from EHR logs

dillon-2025-document-time-no-significant.claim: In the same field RCT, the intent-to-treat effect on time to complete Word documents was a 2% saving, not statistically significant, and an increase of up to 7% could not be ruled out; meeting time also did not change.
dillon-2025-document-time-no-significant.quote: the ITT point estimate is a savings of only 2% of the pre-period mean, and we cannot rule out that document time to complete increased by as much as 7%.

source.title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
source.method: Randomized field experiment across 66 large firms and 7,137 knowledge workers (September 2023 to October 2024); treated workers got Microsoft 365 Copilot in Outlook, Teams, Word and other Office apps; outcomes from Microsoft telemetry over six months, intent-to-treat and LATE estimates

dillon-2025-document-time-no-significant.vendorNote: Microsoft researchers are among the authors, and the tool studied is Microsoft's.

noy-2023-writing-time-down-40-percent.claim: In a preregistered experiment with 453 professionals, access to ChatGPT reduced the average time taken on 20 to 30 minute occupation-specific writing tasks by 40%.
noy-2023-writing-time-down-40-percent.quote: Our results show that ChatGPT substantially raised productivity: The average time taken decreased by 40% and output quality rose by 18%.

source.publisher: Science 381(6654), 187-192; working paper circulated at MIT (March 2023)
source.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
source.method: Preregistered online experiment; 453 college-educated professionals (marketers, grant writers, consultants, data analysts, HR professionals, managers) each did two incentivized 20 to 30 minute occupation-specific writing tasks; half randomly given ChatGPT before the second task

dellacqua-2023-outside-frontier-worse.claim: On a business problem chosen to sit outside GPT-4's capability, consultants using AI were less likely to reach the correct answer than those working without it.
dellacqua-2023-outside-frontier-worse.quote: for a complex managerial task selected to be outside the frontier, subjects using AI were 19% less likely to produce correct solutions compared with those without AI

source.publisher: Organization Science (INFORMS); first circulated as HBS Working Paper 24-013 (2023)
source.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of AI on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
source.method: Preregistered randomized experiment, 758 BCG consultants; no AI vs GPT-4 vs GPT-4 plus prompt-engineering overview; 18 tasks inside the frontier, one strategy task outside it

dellacqua-2023-inside-frontier-gains.claim: On 18 realistic consulting tasks within AI's capability, BCG consultants using GPT-4 completed 12.2% more tasks, 25.1% faster, at significantly higher quality.
dellacqua-2023-inside-frontier-gains.quote: subjects using AI outperformed those not using AI, completing 12.2% more tasks and completing them 25.1% more quickly on average while also delivering solutions of significantly improved quality

source.publisher: Organization Science (INFORMS); first circulated as HBS Working Paper 24-013 (2023)
source.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of AI on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
source.method: Preregistered randomized experiment, 758 BCG consultants; no AI vs GPT-4 vs GPT-4 plus prompt-engineering overview; 18 tasks inside the frontier, one strategy task outside it

dillon-2025-email-time-down-12-percent.claim: Across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers, randomized access to Microsoft 365 Copilot cut time in Outlook email by 1.4 hours per week (12%) on an intent-to-treat basis, and by 2 hours (17%) among actual users.
dillon-2025-email-time-down-12-percent.quote: Intention-to-treat estimates suggest workers with Copilot reduced their time using Outlook for email by 1.4 hours per week, a 12% reduction relative to the pre-period mean. The Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) estimate from instrumenting Copilot use with treatment assignment implies a 2 hour (17%) reduction in Outlook time.

source.title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
source.method: Randomized field experiment across 66 large firms and 7,137 knowledge workers (September 2023 to October 2024); treated workers got Microsoft 365 Copilot in Outlook, Teams, Word and other Office apps; outcomes from Microsoft telemetry over six months, intent-to-treat and LATE estimates

dillon-2025-email-time-down-12-percent.vendorNote: Microsoft researchers are among the authors, and the tool studied is Microsoft's.

brynjolfsson-2023-novices-30-percent.claim: Less skilled and less experienced agents improved on every productivity measure, including roughly 30% more issues resolved per hour, while the most experienced agents saw minimal gains.
brynjolfsson-2023-novices-30-percent.quote: less-skilled and less-experienced workers improve significantly across all productivity measures we consider, including approximate increase of 30% in the number of issues they are able to resolve per hour.

source.publisher: arXiv / NBER Working Paper 31161; published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics (2025)
source.title: Generative AI at Work
source.method: Staggered rollout of a GPT-based conversational assistant to 5,172 customer support agents at one Fortune 500 software firm; difference-in-differences on administrative data

metr-2025-developers-overestimate-speedu.claim: Before the trial developers forecast AI would cut completion time by 24%, and afterward estimated it had cut time by 20%, while the measured effect was a 19% increase.
metr-2025-developers-overestimate-speedu.quote: After completing the study, developers estimate that allowing AI reduced completion time by 20%. Surprisingly, we find that allowing AI actually increases completion time by 19%

source.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
source.method: Randomized controlled trial at the task level; 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 real tasks (about 2 hours each) in mature repositories they had worked on for about 5 years; each task randomly allowed or disallowed AI (mainly Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet); screen recordings

paradis-2024-google-21-percent-faster.claim: In a randomized trial with 96 Google software engineers on an enterprise-grade task, AI assistance cut time on task by about 21%, though the confidence interval is large.
paradis-2024-google-21-percent-faster.quote: Our best estimate of the size of this effect, controlling for factors known to influence developer time on task, stands at about 21%, although our confidence interval is large.

source.title: How much does AI impact development speed? An enterprise-based randomized controlled trial
source.method: Randomized controlled trial with 96 full-time Google software engineers on one complex enterprise-grade task in Google's internal infrastructure; three internal AI features on or off; outcome time on task, controlling for developer and task factors

paradis-2024-google-21-percent-faster.vendorNote: Google studied its own engineers using its own tools.

peng-2023-copilot-55-percent-faster.claim: In a randomized experiment with 95 freelance developers, those given GitHub Copilot completed an HTTP server task in JavaScript 55.8% faster than controls (95% CI 21% to 89%).
peng-2023-copilot-55-percent-faster.quote: The treatment group, with access to the AI pair programmer, completed the task 55.8% faster than the control group.

source.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
source.method: Randomized controlled experiment; 95 freelance developers recruited on Upwork (45 treated, 50 control; 35 completed per arm as reported), one task: implement an HTTP server in JavaScript as fast as possible; outcome is time to completion

peng-2023-copilot-55-percent-faster.vendorNote: GitHub and Microsoft researchers are among the authors, and the tool studied is theirs.

cui-2025-copilot-26-percent-more-tasks.claim: Pooling randomized field experiments at Microsoft, Accenture and a Fortune 100 firm (4,867 developers), access to an AI coding assistant raised completed tasks (pull requests) by 26.08%, with larger gains for less experienced developers.
cui-2025-copilot-26-percent-more-tasks.quote: when data is combined across three experiments and 4,867 developers, our analysis reveals a 26.08% increase (SE: 10.3%) in completed tasks among developers using the AI tool. Notably, less experienced developers had higher adoption rates and greater productivity gains.

source.publisher: Working paper (Princeton, MIT, Microsoft, Wharton), June 2025
source.title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
source.method: Three randomized field experiments run by Microsoft, Accenture and an anonymous Fortune 100 company in the ordinary course of business; 4,867 developers; random subset given an AI coding assistant (GitHub Copilot); main outcome weekly pull requests (completed tasks)

cui-2025-copilot-26-percent-more-tasks.vendorNote: Microsoft researchers are among the authors, and the tool studied is theirs.

humlum-2025-time-savings-by-occupation.claim: Self-reported time savings as a share of total work hours ranged from 0.7% (teachers) to 6.1% (marketing), with software developers at 5.6%, HR and IT support at 3.5%, customer service at 3.0%, legal at 2.6%, office clerks at 2.2%, financial advisors at 1.9% and accountants at 1.6%.
humlum-2025-time-savings-by-occupation.quote: In Column (6), we combine workers' frequency of use with their reported time savings per day of usage to estimate time savings as a percent of total work hours.

source.title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
source.method: Large-scale adoption surveys in 11 AI-exposed occupations linked to Danish administrative labor records; difference-in-differences on earnings and hours

humlum-2025-time-savings-3-percent-of-ho.claim: Combining frequency of use with reported daily time savings, Danish workers in 11 AI-exposed occupations who used chatbots reported saving about 3% of their work hours on average.
humlum-2025-time-savings-3-percent-of-ho.quote: On average, adopters in our sample report savings of about 3% of their work hours. These estimates align with the nationally representative U.S. survey evidence in Bick, Blandin and Deming (2025).

source.title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
source.method: Large-scale adoption surveys in 11 AI-exposed occupations linked to Danish administrative labor records; difference-in-differences on earnings and hours

humlum-2025-null-earnings-effects.claim: Difference-in-differences on Danish records found precise null effects of AI chatbots on earnings and recorded hours, ruling out effects above 2%.
humlum-2025-null-earnings-effects.quote: we estimate precise null effects on earnings and recorded hours at both the worker and workplace levels, ruling out effects larger than 2% two years after the launch of ChatGPT

source.title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
source.method: Large-scale adoption surveys in 11 AI-exposed occupations linked to Danish administrative labor records; difference-in-differences on earnings and hours
